title: Listening
note: This means hearing the learned explain the meaning of the books. It strengthens the knowledge of those who have learned and gives knowledge to those who haven’t, so it follows the chapters on learning and not learning.

couplets.plain: The wealth of wealth is the wealth of the ear. That wealth is first among all wealth.
couplets.pm: The wealth that stands out is the wealth that comes through the ear, knowing all things by listening. It is first of all wealth because other wealth comes from possessions, doesn’t last and ends in suffering. The hint is to leave those and pursue this alone.

links.reason: Gives the ear a wealth of its own, filled by what it hears.
Takes the highest name for wealth and gives it to the ear.

couplets.plain: When there is no food for the ear, give the stomach a little too.
couplets.pm: When there is no listening, the ear’s food, a little is given to the stomach as well. While there is listening, with its great taste and later benefit, food is scorned. A little, because much food means the labour of seeking it, and more illness and desire. Even that is only to stay alive and listen. “Give” shows how low the stomach is.

links.quote: give the stomach a little too
links.reason: Puts food for the ear ahead of a meal, leaving the stomach to wait its turn.

couplets.plain: Those who have listening, the food of the ear, are on this earth the equals of the gods who feed on offerings.
couplets.pm: Those who have listening, the food taken in by the ear, are equal to the gods whose food is offerings, though they live on earth. The gods’ food is given through the sacrificial fire. They are full of understanding and know no suffering, so they are like gods.

links.reason: Makes anyone fed by listening the equal of the gods, here on earth.

couplets.plain: Even if you have no learning, listen. It will be a prop to lean on when you falter.
couplets.pm: Even if you haven’t learned the books that do you good, listen as the learned explain them, because that becomes your support when you falter. Faltering is the mind giving way in trouble, from poverty or lack of understanding, and the knowledge gained by listening removes it. “Even if” means that you should learn as well.

links.quote: Even if you have no learning, listen
links.reason: Opens this road even to someone with no learning, as a prop when they falter.

couplets.plain: The words of people of good conduct are like a staff on slippery ground.
couplets.pm: To those who drive the cart of rule, words from the mouths of people of good conduct help as a staff helps those walking on slippery mud. A staff saves you when you slip. The learned without good conduct are ignorant, so they are not to be listened to. “Mouths” shows that these people know no evil words.

links.quote: like a staff on slippery ground

couplets.plain: Listen to good things, however little. Even that little will bring you full greatness.
couplets.pm: Listen to things that do you good, however little, because even that much brings full greatness. “However little” covers both how much you hear and for how long. Listening gathers like raindrops and gives rise to all knowledge, so don’t scorn it as small.

links.quote: Listen to good things, however little
links.reason: Assures that no amount is too small, since even that little brings greatness.

couplets.plain: Even when they have misunderstood, those who have studied closely and gathered much listening don’t speak folly.
couplets.pm: Even when they grasp something wrongly, they don’t say words that would show folly. These are people who examine things finely themselves and have also gathered listening from many sources. Having tested the truth against those who know, they won’t speak otherwise, even if dullness clouds them.

links.reason: Credits gathered listening with keeping someone from folly even when mistaken.

couplets.plain: Ears not pierced by listening are deaf, even though they hear.
couplets.pm: Ears not bored through by listening may hear sound, which is their field, yet they are deaf. Mere sound brings no benefit. Listening opens the way for the meaning of the books to enter the mind. The old hole isn’t a hole at all.

links.quote: are deaf, even though they hear
links.reason: Declares hearing without listening to be a kind of deafness.
Pictures the ear as something bored through, opened only by listening.

couplets.plain: Those without subtle listening can hardly have humble mouths.
couplets.pm: Those without fine listening can’t have speech that bows, that is, speech that shows humility. Those who don’t listen lack understanding, so they praise themselves.

couplets.plain: People who know the tastes of the mouth but not the tastes of the ear: what does it matter if they die or live?
couplets.pm: People who know only the tastes of the mouth, and not those enjoyed by the ear: what does the world gain or lose if they die or live? The ear’s tastes are the savours of words and of meaning. The mouth’s are the six, such as bitter and sweet. Nothing is lost by their death or gained by their life, so the two are the same.
couplets.sensitive: says some lives make no difference to the world

links.quote: what does it matter if they die or live
links.reason: Says someone with no taste for listening is one the world would hardly notice losing.

ideaLinks.reason: Humble speech is hard to come by without subtle listening.
